requirements.statement: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g) || []; const cats = m.map(s => s.replace(/"category"\s*:\s*"/, '').replace(/"$/, '')); const bad = cats.filter(c => !/^[A-Za-z ]+ – [a-z ]+$/.test(c) && c !== 'Floor – all brands'); return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' category name(s) not in taxonomy form' : 'category names well-formed', spans: [] }; }
means: Checks each category name has the 'Family – variant' form; the full 39-name list is not in the outline, so exact membership is left to the person.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a timecode span, start–end in mm:ss, inside the clip's duration.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*–\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s = +m[1]*60+ +m[2]; const e = +m[3]*60+ +m[4]; if (!(e > s)) bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index+m[0].length, why: 'span end not after start'}); } const d = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); const dur = d ? +d[1]*60+ +d[2] : null; if (dur !== null) { const re2 = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*–\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; while ((m = re2.exec(text))) { const e = +m[3]*60+ +m[4]; if (e > dur) bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index+m[0].length, why: 'span runs past duration'}); } } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' bad span(s)' : 'spans are in mm:ss, ordered and inside duration', spans: bad }; }
means: Each span is read as mm:ss start–end; the check flags spans whose end is not after the start or that run past the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a risk level: Low, Medium or High.

source: (text) => {
const bad = [];
let m;
while ((m = re.exec(text))) {
if (!/^(Low|Medium|High)$/.test(m[1])) {
bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'risk not Low, Medium or High'});
return {
ok: bad.length === 0,
detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' flagged item(s) with invalid risk' : 'every flagged category has a valid risk',
spans: bad
means: Each flagged category entry must carry a risk value that is Low, Medium or High.

requirements.statement: "High" risk requires an explicit depiction in the clip: a described act, injury, blood, a weapon fired, an explicit sexual act. A reference, a mention or a discussion is Medium at most.
A clip labelled "Firearms – depiction" or "Firearms – use" is never also labelled "Floor – all brands".

source: (text) => { const hasFire = /Firearms – (depiction|use)/.test(text); const hasFloor = /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const ok = !(hasFire && hasFloor); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'no conflicting firearm and floor labels' : 'firearm label appears with Floor – all brands', spans: ok ? [] : [{start: text.search(/Floor – all brands/), end: text.search(/Floor – all brands/)+'Floor – all brands'.length, why: 'Floor label alongside firearm label'}] }; }
means: The label text is searched for a firearm category and the Floor label together; both together fail.

requirements.statement: A clip with no flagged category is labelled "Floor – all brands" with risk Floor and no timecode.

source: (text) => { const hasCats = /"category"\s*:/.test(text); const floor = /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const noRisk = /"overall"\s*:\s*"Floor"/.test(text); if (hasCats) return { ok: true, detail: 'clip has flagged categories; rule does not apply', spans: [] }; const ok = floor && noRisk && !/"span"/.test(text); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'unflagged clip labelled Floor with no span' : 'unflagged clip not labelled Floor – all brands with Floor risk and no span', spans: [] }; }
means: If the label has no flagged category, it must read Floor – all brands, overall Floor, with no span.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.
"Violence – graphic" requires described injury or blood; a scuffle, a push or a threat is "Violence – minor".
"Language – strong" requires a word of the strong list in the transcript; "Language – mild" otherwise.
A label carries no category the transcript does not support with evidence.
Risk is the highest of the flagged categories' risk levels, carried once at the top of the label as overall.

source: (text) => { const rank = {Floor:0, Low:1, Medium:2, High:3}; const o = text.match(/"overall"\s*:\s*"(\w+)"/); const risks = [...text.matchAll(/"risk"\s*:\s*"(\w+)"/g)].map(x => x[1]); if (!o) return { ok: false, detail: 'no overall value', spans: [] }; if (!risks.length) return { ok: rank[o[1]] === 0, detail: 'no flagged risks; overall should be Floor', spans: [] }; const max = risks.reduce((a,b) => rank[b] > rank[a] ? b : a, risks[0]); const ok = o[1] === max; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'overall equals highest flagged risk' : 'overall ' + o[1] + ' differs from highest risk ' + max, spans: [] }; }
means: The overall value is compared with the highest risk among the flagged categories.

requirements.statement: A span's end is after its start, and no span runs past the duration.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*–\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s = +m[1]*60+ +m[2]; const e = +m[3]*60+ +m[4]; if (!(e > s)) bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index+m[0].length, why: 'end not after start'}); } const d = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); if (d) { const dur = +d[1]*60+ +d[2]; const re2 = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*–\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; while ((m = re2.exec(text))) { const e = +m[3]*60+ +m[4]; if (e > dur) bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index+m[0].length, why: 'span past duration'}); } } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' span problem(s)' : 'spans ordered and within duration', spans: bad }; }
means: Each span end is compared with its start and with the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Where the same act is both "Violence" and "Dangerous acts", both are flagged, each with its own evidence.
A news report of a disaster is "Disaster – news", Medium at most; graphic footage described is "Disaster – graphic".
A reference to alcohol in passing is "Alcohol – reference", Low; drinking described is "Alcohol – consumption", Medium.
Numbers in a span are seconds and minutes only: no frame counts.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"[^"]*"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { if (/frame/i.test(m[0]) || /\d+\s*f\b/.test(m[0])) bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index+m[0].length, why: 'frame count in span'}); } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? 'frame count found in span' : 'no frame counts in spans', spans: bad }; }
means: Spans are checked for any frame count wording or frame-suffixed number.

requirements.statement: Evidence is copied from the transcript, never paraphrased.
A category flagged twice is listed once, with the earliest span.

source: (text) => { const cats = [...text.matchAll(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g)].map(m => m[1]); const seen = {}; const bad = []; for (const c of cats) { if (seen[c]) bad.push({start: text.indexOf('"'+c+'"'), end: text.indexOf('"'+c+'"')+c.length+2, why: 'category listed twice'}); seen[c] = true; } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' duplicate category entries' : 'each category listed once', spans: bad }; }
means: Each category name appears at most once in the categories list; a repeat is flagged.

requirements.statement: The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.

source: (text) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return { ok: false, detail: 'label is not valid JSON', spans: [] }; } const keys = Object.keys(obj).sort().join(','); const ok = keys === 'categories,clip,duration,overall'; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'label has exactly the four keys' : 'keys are ' + keys, spans: [] }; }
means: The label must parse as JSON and have exactly the keys clip, duration, overall and categories.

requirements.statement: Where a clip's transcript is empty, the label is "Floor – all brands" and says so in evidence.

source: (text) => { const floor = /"category"\s*:\s*"Floor – all brands"/.test(text) || /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const says = /transcript/i.test(text); const ok = !floor || says; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'empty-transcript rule held or not applicable' : 'Floor label without saying transcript is empty', spans: [] }; }
means: If the label is Floor – all brands, the evidence must say the transcript is empty; whether the transcript was empty is not visible in the label text alone.

requirements.statement: My pieces run 224 to 452 characters; a new piece stays between 1 and 680.
My pieces run 23 to 53 words; a new piece stays between 1 and 83.
My pieces run 1 sentence; a new piece has at most 2.
The longest sentence in my pieces runs 23 to 53 words; in a new piece it stays at most 83 words.
At most 24 line breaks: my pieces carry 12 to 18.
No blank lines: none of my pieces has one.
No hashtags: none of my pieces has one.
No mentions (@): none of my pieces has one.
No links: none of my pieces has one.
No emoji: none of my pieces has one.
Open on a claim, as my pieces do.
Close on a statement, as my pieces do.
The first word is a symbol or emoji, as in every piece of mine.
Quoted phrases: about 53 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Colons: about 28.2 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Figures written in digits: about 20.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Nominalisations (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ence): about 8.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Runs of five or more one-syllable words: about 2.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
I keep paragraphs to 2 sentences at most.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.

evidence: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.
Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.
The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.
